page.overview:
Who is Neal Carter?

Neal Carter (born 30 August 1923 and died 23 April 2019) was an American racing driver who racing midget cars in the United States. He entered the 1952 Indianapolis 500, but failed to qualify for the event.

Carter began his career in a midget car he had purchased with a loan from his mother, although his mother believed the loan was for a road car. He raced largely in midget cars until retiring in 1955 to raise a family.

During the 1980s, he was instrumental in medical and safety advancements in American single-seat racing. He was also involved in the construction of a midget racing circuit in Ohio. He also worked as a service manager for a variety of American car dealerships after retiring from racing.

Carter appeared in the historic car display at the 2011 Indianapolis 500 to celebrate the 100th running of the race.
